b: The 2026 edition of the Italian furniture components exhibition welcomed 29,703 attendees, with international visitors accounting for 41% of the total.
SICAM 2026 brought together furniture industry professionals from 125 countries at the Pordenone Fiere in Italy

The 17th edition of SICAM, the International Exhibition of Components, Semi-finished Products and Accessories for the Furniture Industry, attracted 29,703 attendees from 125 countries, according to figures released by the organiser.

Held at the Pordenone Fiere in Italy from 20 to 23 Oct, the event brought together furniture industry professionals to explore new products, materials and technologies across 41,000 sq m of exhibition space, including 19,150 sq m of net exhibition space.

Carolina Giobbi, SICAM’s head of marketing and communications, described the 2026 edition as an “excellent” event, highlighting the quality of business contacts and the range of new products on display.

“The sheer number of new products and ideas gave us a preview of the trends that will shape the furniture industry in the seasons ahead,” she said. “Above all, they showed how committed the industry is to building its future after a challenging period.”
Visitors explored components, semi-finished products and accessories presented by 698 exhibitors across the four-day event

Of the 29,703 attendees, 24,100 were visitors and 5,603 were exhibitors. Visitors spent an average of 1.33 days at the event, with Italian trade professionals averaging 1.19 days and international visitors 1.61 days.
A total of 9,450 companies visited the stands of the 698 exhibitors. International exhibitors accounted for 31% of the total and came from 34 countries.
International visitors made up 41% of all visitors. Europe accounted for 70% of this group, followed by Asia at 20%, the Americas at 5%, Africa at 4% and Oceania at 1%.
Germany was the leading source of international visitors, followed by Slovenia, Spain, Croatia, Poland, China, Austria, the UK, Türkiye and France.
Among Italian trade visitors, Veneto accounted for the largest share at 30%, followed by Friuli Venezia Giulia at 21%, Lombardy at 15%, Marche at 6% and Emilia-Romagna at 5%.
SICAM provided a platform for industry professionals to meet, discuss new developments and explore business opportunities across the furniture supply chain

The organiser said the exhibition provided opportunities for business meetings and exchanges across the furniture supply chain. Its layout was designed to help visitors navigate the venue and explore the range of products and solutions presented by exhibitors.

Sustainability was also a prominent theme across the exhibition, reflecting its growing role in the furniture industry. Meetings and seminars organised during the event addressed opportunities in new markets, the importance of engaging and training younger generations, and the implications of innovative manufacturing processes.

The city of Pordenone also welcomed exhibitors and visitors through the latest edition of Enjoy Pordenone with SICAM, a programme of meetings and events highlighting the city and its cultural offerings ahead of the 2027 exhibition, which will coincide with Pordenone’s year as Italian Capital of Culture.

Preparations for the next edition are already under way, with SICAM continuing its international promotional programme at major events across the furniture supply chain. Following FIMMA + Maderalia in Valencia, the exhibition is scheduled to participate in FIND Design Fair Asia in Bangkok from 26 to 28 Nov.
According to the organiser, several exhibitors had already confirmed their return for 2027 before the 2026 edition had closed.
The 18th edition of SICAM will take place from 19 to 22 Oct 2027.
